body.translated_text: 1. Brahmakāṇḍa (The Chapter on Brahman)

children.translated_text: from which the activity of the world proceeds, manifesting in the form of meaning — [this is described]. // 1.1 //

body.translated_text: Brahman, without beginning or end, whose essence is the Word (śabdatattva), the imperishable,

children.translated_text: though not distinct from its powers, appears as though separate [from them]. // 1.2 //

body.translated_text: That which is one alone, as taught in scripture, by virtue of dependence on diverse powers,

children.translated_text: the six modifications beginning with birth are the sources of differentiation in existence. // 1.3 //

body.translated_text: Relying on the power of time (kālaśakti), with its portions superimposed,

children.translated_text: existence takes the form of enjoyer, enjoyed, and enjoyment — // 1.4 //

body.translated_text: Of that one, the seed of all, whose manifold

children.translated_text: though one, it was taught separately, as if following many paths. // 1.5 //

body.translated_text: The Veda is the means of attaining that [Brahman] and its reflection; by the great sages,

children.translated_text: and the limited power of words — these are seen in its branches (śākhās). // 1.6 //

body.translated_text: The multiplicity of paths among the divisions, the subordination of parts to a single ritual action,

children.translated_text: were devised by those who know the <s>Veda</s>, based on inferential signs (<s>liṅgas</s>), relying on that [<s>Brahman</s>] alone. // 1.7 //

body.translated_text: And the <s>smṛtis</s> (traditional texts), of many forms, having both seen and unseen purposes,

children.translated_text: the doctrines of monists and dualists have come about in many ways. // 1.8 //

body.translated_text: Of that [<s>Brahman</s>], in the form of <s>arthavāda</s> (explanatory passages), arising from their own conceptual constructions,

children.translated_text: joined with the form of <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ), which is not contradicted by any doctrine. // 1.9 //

body.translated_text: True purification is declared therein, knowledge alone being the single-word revelation,

children.translated_text: the branches of knowledge are extended, serving as causes of the purification of understanding. // 1.10 //

body.translated_text: Of that creator of the worlds, based on major and minor limbs,

body.text: āsannaṃ brahmaṇas tasya $ tapasām uttamaṃ tapaḥ &

children.text: prathamaṃ chandasām aṅgam % āhur vyākaraṇaṃ budhāḥ // 1.11 //
children.translated_text: the wise declare grammar (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>) to be the foremost limb of the <s>Vedas</s>. // 1.11 //

body.translated_text: Close to that <s>Brahman</s>, the highest of austerities,

children.text: yat tat puṇyatamaṃ jyotis % tasya mārgo 'yam āñjasaḥ // 1.12 //
children.translated_text: to that most sacred light, this [grammar] is the direct path. // 1.12 //

body.translated_text: For speech that has attained the distinction of form, there is a supreme essence;

children.translated_text: knowledge of the true nature of words does not exist apart from grammar (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>). // 1.13 //

body.translated_text: Words alone are the basis for the operation of the true nature of things;

children.translated_text: the purifier of all sciences, it shines as the supreme knowledge. // 1.14 //

body.translated_text: That [grammar] is the gateway to liberation (<s>apavarga</s>), the remedy for the impurities of speech,

children.text: tathaiva loke vidyānām % eṣā vidyā parāyaṇam // 1.15 //
children.translated_text: so too in the world, among all sciences, this science is the ultimate foundation. // 1.15 //

body.translated_text: Just as all classes of objects are grounded in the forms of words,

children.translated_text: this is the straight royal path for those who seek liberation. // 1.16 //

body.translated_text: This is the primary abode of words, the steps on the stairway to perfection;

children.text: chandasyaś chandasāṃ yonim % ātmā chandomayīṃ tanum // 1.17 //
children.translated_text: the self of the Vedic sage sees the source of the <s>Vedas</s>, the form made of sacred meters. // 1.17 //

body.translated_text: Here, one who has transcended error perceives only the pure [reality];

children.text: yad asminn eva tamasi % jyotiḥ śuddhaṃ vivartate // 1.18 //
children.translated_text: in this very darkness, pure light manifests. // 1.18 //

body.translated_text: That supreme form of speech in which all distinctions have set,

children.translated_text: having gone beyond light and darkness, they worship that radiance. // 1.19 //

body.translated_text: Having transcended the modified state, the perception of activities involving form,

children.translated_text: shine forth like reflections through a yoga preceded by the Word. // 1.20 //

body.translated_text: Where the indicators of speech, like signs of recollected syllables,

children.translated_text: in which the high and low syllables (<s>varṇas</s>) stand separately, each grasped individually. // 1.21 //

body.translated_text: Of the <s>Atharvan</s>, <s>Āṅgirasa</s>, <s>Sāman</s>, <s>Ṛk</s>, and <s>Yajus</s>,

children.translated_text: by approaching grammar, the supreme <s>Brahman</s> is realized. // 1.22 //

body.translated_text: That which is one, divided in many ways through differences of grammatical analysis —

children.translated_text: who are the authors of the <s>sūtras</s> along with their subsidiary works and commentaries. // 1.23 //

body.translated_text: The eternal relationships between words and meanings, taught therein by the great sages,

children.text: anvākhyeyāś ca ye śabdā % ye cāpi pratipādakāḥ // 1.24 //
children.translated_text: and those words that are to be explained and those that are the means of explanation — // 1.24 //

body.translated_text: Those meanings that are abstracted and those meanings that have established characteristics,

children.text: dharme ye pratyaye cāṅgaṃ % saṃbandhāḥ sādhvasādhuṣu // 1.25 //
children.translated_text: and those connections which are subsidiary to <s>dharma</s> and to understanding, in the correct and incorrect [usages] — // 1.25 //

body.translated_text: standing in the relationship of cause and effect, and in the relationship of fitness,

body.text: te liṅgaiś ca svaśabdaiś ca $ śāstre 'sminn upavarṇitāḥ &

children.text: smṛtyartham anugamyante % ke cid eva yathāgamam // 1.26 //
children.translated_text: only some of them are traced according to tradition for the purpose of remembrance. // 1.26 //

body.translated_text: these are described in this treatise by means of inferential signs and specific terms;

children.translated_text: the incorrect ones are those that are opposite, without any difference in conveying meaning. // 1.27 //

body.translated_text: The correct forms, established from the learned through tradition, are the means of <s>dharma</s>;

body.text: nityatve kṛtakatve vā $ teṣām ādir na vidyate &

children.translated_text: like that of living beings, this is called a conventional permanence. // 1.28 //

body.translated_text: Whether they are eternal or produced, their beginning is not known;

body.text: nānarthikām imāṃ kaś cid $ vyavasthāṃ kartum arhati &

children.translated_text: therefore, a tradition concerning correctness is composed by the learned. // 1.29 //

body.translated_text: No one can make this arrangement purposeless;

body.text: na cāgamād ṛte dharmas $ tarkeṇa vyavatiṣṭhate &

children.text: ṛṣīṇām api yaj jñānaṃ % tad apy āgamapūrvakam // 1.30 //
children.translated_text: even the knowledge of the sages is preceded by scripture (<s>āgama</s>). // 1.30 //

body.translated_text: And without scripture, <s>dharma</s> cannot be established by reasoning alone;

children.text: na tāṃl lokaprasiddhatvāt % kaś cit tarkeṇa bādhate // 1.31 //
children.translated_text: no one can obstruct them by reasoning, because they are well-known in the world. // 1.31 //

body.translated_text: And the unbroken paths of <s>dharma</s> that are established —

children.translated_text: the establishment of things through inference alone is extremely difficult to obtain. // 1.32 //

body.translated_text: Due to the differences of condition, place, and time, when powers are differentiated,

body.text: nirjñātaśakter dravyasya $ tāṃ tām arthakriyāṃ prati &

children.translated_text: that power is obstructed when connected with a different substance. // 1.33 //

body.translated_text: For a substance whose power has been ascertained with respect to a particular purposive action,

children.translated_text: is demonstrated otherwise by others who are more proficient. // 1.34 //

body.translated_text: A meaning inferred with effort even by skilled reasoners

children.translated_text: for those who possess such knowledge, it is not inferential. // 1.35 //

body.translated_text: The knowledge of gems, silver, and the like arises in others only through practice, without being explicitly taught;

children.translated_text: the powers of ancestors, <s>Rakṣas</s> (demons), and <s>Piśācas</s> (spirits) arise from their past actions alone. // 1.36 //

body.translated_text: Transcending both perception and inference,

children.translated_text: knowledge of past and future is not different from direct perception. // 1.37 //

body.translated_text: For those whose light has become manifest, whose minds are unclouded,

children.text: ye bhāvān vacanaṃ teṣāṃ % nānumānena bādhyate // 1.38 //
children.translated_text: their utterance is not contradicted by inference. // 1.38 //

body.translated_text: Those who see supersensory, imperceptible things with the eye of the sages (<s>ārṣa cakṣus</s>) —

body.text: yo yasya svam iva jñānaṃ $ darśanaṃ nātiśaṅkate &

children.text: thitaṃ pratyakṣapakṣe taṃ % katham anyo nivartayet // 1.39 //
children.translated_text: established in the side of direct perception — how can another dissuade him? // 1.39 //

body.translated_text: One who does not doubt the knowledge of another, as if it were one's own perception,

body.text: idaṃ puṇyam idaṃ pāpam $ ity etasmin padadvaye &

children.translated_text: for all human beings down to the <s>Caṇḍāla</s>, the purpose of scripture is small. // 1.40 //

body.translated_text: "This is meritorious, this is sinful" — with regard to this pair of concepts,

body.text: caitanyam iva yaś cāyam $ avicchedena vartate &

children.text: āgamas tam upāsīno % hetuvādair na bādhyate // 1.41 //
children.translated_text: one who relies on that tradition is not overturned by arguments. // 1.41 //

body.translated_text: And like consciousness, this [tradition] that continues without interruption —

children.translated_text: for one who relies primarily on inference, a downfall is not hard to come by. // 1.42 //

body.translated_text: Like a blind man running on an uneven path by the touch of a hand,

body.text: tasmād akṛtakaṃ śāstraṃ $ smṛtiṃ ca sanibandhanām &

children.translated_text: the learned compose a tradition regarding correctness. // 1.43 //

body.translated_text: Therefore, relying on uncreated scripture and well-founded <s>smṛti</s>,

children.translated_text: one is the ground of [other] words, the other is employed for meaning. // 1.44 //

body.translated_text: In the designating words, those who know words recognize two kinds of word:

children.translated_text: therein, the word whose nature is the form of meaning undergoes fusion. // 1.45 //

body.translated_text: From the undivided, the word that denotes meaning is born from the divided [elements];

body.text: ātmabhedaṃ tayoḥ ke cid $ astīty āhuḥ purāṇagāḥ &

children.translated_text: others declare a difference in what is undifferentiated, due to a difference in cognition. // 1.46 //

body.translated_text: Some followers of the ancients say that there is an essential difference between the two;

children.text: tadvac chabdo 'pi buddhisthaḥ % śrutīnāṃ kāraṇaṃ pṛthak // 1.47 //
children.translated_text: so too the word residing in the mind is separately the cause of audible sounds. // 1.47 //

body.translated_text: Just as light residing in the fire-stick (<s>araṇi</s>) is the cause of another manifestation of light,

body.text: vitarkitaḥ purā buddhyā $ kva cid arthe niveśitaḥ &

children.translated_text: it is supported by the sound (<s>dhvani</s>) that issues forth from the organs [of speech]. // 1.48 //

body.translated_text: Previously conceived by the intellect, applied to some meaning,

body.text: nādasya kramajātatvān $ na pūrvo na paraś ca saḥ &

children.translated_text: being without sequence, it appears as though differentiated in sequential form. // 1.49 //

body.translated_text: Since sound (<s>nāda</s>) is produced sequentially, it is neither prior nor subsequent;

children.translated_text: seems to follow the movement [of the water] — such is the relation between <s>sphoṭa</s> and <s>nāda</s>. // 1.50 //

body.translated_text: Just as a reflection situated elsewhere, due to the action of water,

body.text: ātmarūpaṃ yathā jñāne $ jñeyarūpaṃ ca dṛśyate &

children.text: artharūpaṃ tathā śabde % svarūpaṃ ca prakāśate // 1.51 //
children.translated_text: so too in the word, both the form of the meaning and its own form are manifested. // 1.51 //

body.translated_text: Just as in cognition, both the form of the self and the form of the known object are seen,

children.text: vṛttis tasya kriyārūpā % bhāgaśo bhajate kramam // 1.52 //
children.translated_text: its activity, in the form of action, partakes of sequence part by part. // 1.52 //

body.translated_text: That intention (<s>kratu</s>) called 'word,' which has assumed an egg-like form,

children.translated_text: so too a triad [of differences] of another form is seen in the word. // 1.53 //

body.translated_text: Just as a figure that is the object of a single cognition is depicted on a canvas,

body.text: yathā prayoktuḥ prāg buddhiḥ $ śabdeṣv eva pravartate &

children.text: vyavasāyo grahītṝṇām % evaṃ teṣv eva jāyate // 1.54 //
children.translated_text: so too the determination of the listeners arises in those very [words]. // 1.54 //

body.translated_text: Just as the cognition of the speaker first operates upon the words,

children.translated_text: are not apprehended by ordinary people as serving another purpose. // 1.55 //

body.translated_text: Those [words] that have become subordinate to meaning, having fulfilled their purpose in certain denotations,

body.text: grāhyatvaṃ grāhakatvaṃ ca $ dve śaktī tejaso yathā &

children.translated_text: so too all words have these two [powers], standing separately. // 1.56 //

body.translated_text: Just as light has two powers — that of being perceived and that of perceiving —

children.translated_text: they are not illuminators of meanings when they are unapprehended, by their mere existence. // 1.57 //

body.translated_text: The meaning is not illuminated by words that have not become objects [of cognition];

children.translated_text: The own-form of sense objects is not apprehended by the senses in the same way. // 1.58 //

body.translated_text: Therefore, because their form is not fully known, it is said, 'What does he say?'

children.translated_text: serve as causes in the effects of differentiation without contradiction. // 1.59 //

body.translated_text: Two properties of the word, apprehended through differentiation and abstracted,

children.translated_text: they enter into relationship with the designata indicated by words like '<s>āt</s>' and others. // 1.60 //

body.translated_text: Just as words like <s>vṛddhi</s> and others are grounded in their own form,

children.translated_text: enters into relationship through the utterance of '<s>agni</s>' with the referent designated by the word '<s>agni</s>'. // 1.61 //

body.translated_text: Similarly, this word '<s>agni</s>' (fire), grounded in the word '<s>agni</s>',

body.text: yo ya uccāryate śabdo $ niyataṃ na sa kāryabhāk &

children.translated_text: its power to convey another [meaning] is not obstructed. // 1.62 //

body.translated_text: Whatever word is uttered, it is not necessarily subject to [grammatical] operations;

body.text: uccaran paratantratvād $ guṇaḥ kāryair na yujyate &

children.translated_text: therefore, the connection of operations is conceived through the meanings of those [words]. // 1.63 //

body.translated_text: The quality [of sound], being dependent [on the speaker], is not associated with [grammatical] operations;

children.translated_text: in those analogies, another property [always] differs. // 1.64 //

body.translated_text: Whatever commonality is shared between the exemplar and the exemplified,

children.translated_text: from that very quality on which it depends, superiority is understood. // 1.65 //

body.translated_text: A quality that is independently taught as the cause of excellence —

children.text: tasyāpy uccāraṇe rūpam % anyat tasmād vivicyate // 1.66 //
children.translated_text: in its utterance too, another form is distinguished from it. // 1.66 //

body.translated_text: The word that stands as the denotatum of that [<s>sphoṭa</s>],

children.text: ṣaṣṭhyāś ca prathamāyāś ca % nimittatvāya kalpate // 1.67 //
children.translated_text: it serves as the basis for both the genitive and the nominative [case relations]. // 1.67 //

body.translated_text: Before the connection with the designatum, the <s>saṃjñā</s> (technical name) has its meaning in its own form;

children.text: asyeti vyatirekaś ca % tadarthād eva jāyate // 1.68 //
children.translated_text: and the distinction expressed by 'of this' also arises from that very meaning. // 1.68 //

body.translated_text: Because the nominative has meaning, it is enjoined from the <s>saṃjñā</s> word;

body.text: svaṃ rūpam iti kaiś cit tu $ vyaktiḥ saṃjñopadiśyate &

children.text: jāteḥ kāryāṇi saṃsṛṣṭā % jātis tu pratipadyate // 1.69 //
children.translated_text: the universal (<s>jāti</s>) undergoes the operations associated [with it], but the <s>jāti</s> itself is understood. // 1.69 //

body.translated_text: But some teach that [what is designated by] 'one's own form' is the individual (<s>vyakti</s>) as the <s>saṃjñā</s>;

body.text: saṃjñinīṃ vyaktim icchanti $ sūtre grāhyām athāpare &

children.translated_text: the individual indicated by the universal is what applies in specific contexts. // 1.70 //

body.translated_text: Others wish that it is the individual (<s>vyakti</s>) as the <s>saṃjñin</s> (bearer of the name) that is to be grasped in the <s>sūtra</s>;

body.text: kāryatve nityatāyāṃ vā $ ke cid ekatvavādinaḥ &

children.text: kāryatve nityatāyāṃ vā % ke cin nānātvavādinaḥ // 1.71 //
children.translated_text: others maintain the multiplicity [of the word], whether it be produced or eternal. // 1.71 //

body.translated_text: Some maintain the unity [of the word], whether it be produced or eternal;

children.text: vākyeṣu padam ekaṃ ca % bhinneṣv apy upalabhyate // 1.72 //
children.translated_text: and a single word is perceived even in different sentences. // 1.72 //

body.translated_text: Even when words differ, the unity of phonemes (<s>varṇas</s>) does not cease;

body.text: na varṇavyatirekeṇa $ padam anyac ca vidyate &

children.text: vākyaṃ varṇapadābhyāṃ ca % vyatiriktaṃ na kiṃ ca na // 1.73 //
children.translated_text: and a sentence is nothing apart from its phonemes and words. // 1.73 //

body.translated_text: There is no word that exists apart from its phonemes;

body.text: pade na varṇā vidyante $ varṇeṣv avayavā na ca &

children.text: vākyāt padānām atyantaṃ % pravibhāgo na kaś ca na // 1.74 //
children.translated_text: from the sentence, there is no absolute separation of words. // 1.74 //

body.translated_text: In the word, phonemes do not [truly] exist, and in phonemes, there are no parts;

children.text: tatra yan mukhyam ekeṣāṃ % tatrānyeṣāṃ viparyayaḥ // 1.75 //
children.translated_text: what is primary for some is the reverse for others. // 1.75 //

body.translated_text: Practice is followed based on adopting different viewpoints;

children.translated_text: They declare the difference of function (<s>vṛtti</s>) based on the difference of the conditions of apprehension. // 1.76 //

body.translated_text: Of the <s>sphoṭa</s>, whose time is undivided, conforming to the time of <s>dhvani</s>,

children.translated_text: the time of the natural <s>dhvani</s> (sound) is figuratively attributed to <s>śabda</s> (the word). // 1.77 //

body.translated_text: With regard to the natural distinctions in the eternal [sounds] — short, long, <s>pluta</s> (protracted), and so on —

body.text: śabdasya grahaṇe hetuḥ $ prākṛto dhvanir iṣyate &

children.translated_text: while the modified [<s>dhvani</s>] serves as the ground for the differentiation of states. // 1.78 //

body.translated_text: The natural <s>dhvani</s> is held to be the cause of the apprehension of <s>śabda</s>,

children.text: dhvanayaḥ samupohante % sphoṭātmā tair na bhidyate // 1.79 //
children.translated_text: <s>dhvanis</s> (sounds) accumulate differences of function, but the <s>sphoṭa</s>-essence is not differentiated by them. // 1.79 //

body.translated_text: After the manifestation of <s>śabda</s>, the modified

children.translated_text: these are the three positions of the proponents of manifestation (<s>abhivyaktivādin</s>). // 1.80 //

body.translated_text: The <s>dhvanis</s> produce an impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) either on the sense organ alone, or on <s>śabda</s> alone, or on both —

children.translated_text: but the impression on the object [is] for the apprehension of its subtle quality. // 1.81 //

body.translated_text: The impression on the sense organ [is produced] by means such as concentration and collyrium,

body.text: cakṣuṣaḥ prāpyakāritve $ tejasā tu dvayor api &

children.text: viṣayendriyayor iṣṭaḥ % saṃskāraḥ sa kramo dhvaneḥ // 1.82 //
children.translated_text: the impression on both object and sense organ is accepted — that is the sequence of <s>dhvani</s>. // 1.82 //

body.translated_text: If the eye operates by reaching [its object], then through light,

children.text: kaiś cid dhvanir asaṃvedyaḥ % svatantro 'nyaiḥ prakalpitaḥ // 1.83 //
children.translated_text: while others conceive <s>dhvani</s> as imperceptible and independent. // 1.83 //

body.translated_text: Some hold that the apprehension of <s>dhvani</s> is inseparable from the <s>sphoṭa</s>-form,

children.text: āvṛttyā na tu sa granthaḥ % pratyāvṛtti nirūpyate // 1.84 //
children.translated_text: yet the text (<s>grantha</s>) is not determined by each repetition. // 1.84 //

body.translated_text: Just as a Vedic passage (<s>anuvāka</s>) or a verse (<s>śloka</s>) can be recited [repeatedly],

children.translated_text: the essential form of <s>śabda</s> is ascertained when illuminated by <s>dhvani</s>. // 1.85 //

body.translated_text: Through cognitions that are inexpressible, yet conducive to apprehension,

children.translated_text: and which has matured through repetition, <s>śabda</s> is ascertained. // 1.86 //

body.translated_text: In the intellect wherein the seed has been planted by the <s>nāda</s>s (sounds), together with the final <s>dhvani</s>,

body.text: asataś cāntarāle yāñ $ śabdān astīti manyate &

children.text: pratipattur aśaktiḥ sā % grahaṇopāya eva saḥ // 1.87 //
children.translated_text: that is the incapacity of the perceiver; those are merely the means of apprehension. // 1.87 //

body.translated_text: And the sounds which one thinks exist in the intermediate [stages] though they are unreal —

children.translated_text: speech has a form invested with sequence, while cognition depends on the object of knowledge. // 1.88 //

body.translated_text: Differentiation is an inevitable imitation in cognition and an overflow of speech;

children.translated_text: nor is any meaning expressed by speech that has not acquired sequence.] // 1.89 //

body.translated_text: [Cognition without the object of knowledge does not stand firm in practical usage,

children.translated_text: of other numbers, even though they are different, so too is the hearing of other words. // 1.90 //

body.translated_text: Just as the apprehension of the first number is the means for the understanding

children.translated_text: yet despite their absolute difference, their powers appear as if commingled. // 1.91 //

body.translated_text: The individual manifesting agents (<s>vyañjaka</s>s) in <s>varṇa</s>s (phonemes), sentences, and words are distinct,

body.text: yathaiva darśanaiḥ pūrvair $ dūrāt saṃtamase 'pi vā &

children.translated_text: one modifies the object and then ascertains it in a different way, // 1.92 //

body.translated_text: Just as through previous perceptions, from a distance or even in darkness,

children.translated_text: the intellect first operates in the form of partial apprehension. // 1.93 //

body.translated_text: so too, when a sentence is being manifested by the causes of sentence-manifestation,

children.translated_text: so too is the sequence in the cognitions of perceivers fixed. // 1.94 //

body.translated_text: Just as the sequence is fixed in the transformation of milk and seed,

body.text: bhāgavatsv api teṣv eva $ rūpabhedo dhvaneḥ kramāt &

children.translated_text: or else, the imputation of part-distinctions is a means [of understanding] for what is truly partless. // 1.95 //

body.translated_text: In those very [units] that appear to have parts, the differentiation of form arises from the sequence of <s>dhvani</s>;

children.text: kaiś cid vyaktaya evāsyā % dhvanitvena prakalpitāḥ // 1.96 //

children.text: sunv abhīty ābhimukhye ca % kevalo 'pi prayujyate // 2.201 //

children.translated_text: while for some, their powers are inferred through co-occurrence and non-occurrence. (2.209)

children.text: ātvādīnāṃ hi śuddhānāṃ % laukiko 'rtho na vidyate // 2.210 //

children.text: prāg vibhaktes tadantasya % tathaivārtho na vidyate // 2.211 //

children.translated_text: is understood as such by virtue of the context of meaningfulness. (2.212)

body.text: ātmabhedo na cet kaś cid $ varṇebhyaḥ padavākyayoḥ &

body.translated_text: When the aggregate and its parts have different meanings in formations,

body.translated_text: Just as in <s>ekaśeṣa</s> (retention of one), <s>bhuj</s> and the like apply to each individual,

children.translated_text: that too has the same form as a pronoun referring to a meaning from which something is excluded. (2.223)

children.translated_text: so too is the sequential perception in the parts of the <s>dvandva</s> compound's meaning. (2.224)

body.translated_text: Just as particular actions initiated in one part of a group are considered

children.text: prādhānyaṃ bahudhā bhāṣye % doṣās tu prakriyāgatāḥ // 2.227 //

children.translated_text: the abandonment of the entire meaning of the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound's words is shown. (2.228)

body.translated_text: And in the alternative where the original meaning is abandoned, by one wishing for complete abandonment,

children.translated_text: those are stated as base-meanings in another tradition. (2.231)

body.translated_text: And the meanings of suffixes that are based on the memory of etymological explanation —

children.translated_text: since the procedures of the <s>śāstra</s>'s meaning are considered to be for practical use. (2.232)

body.translated_text: '<s>Udvamikarī</s>' is said thus in the <s>śāstra</s> on the basis of established usage,

children.translated_text: but <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), which is beyond the alternatives not based on tradition, arises by itself. (2.233)

children.translated_text: so too <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), though inexpressible, is perceived as if through the means of the <s>śāstra</s>. (2.234)

body.translated_text: Just as a fruit, unattached to causes and indescribable,

body.text: yathābhyāsaṃ hi vāg arthe $ pratipattiṃ samīhate &

children.translated_text: and false practice is established as if it were innate nature, beginningless. (2.235)

body.translated_text: For speech seeks to convey meaning in accordance with practice,

children.translated_text: and similarly imagines a composite entity as connected with other parts. (2.236)

children.text: samārambhāc ca bhāvānām % ādimad brahma śāśvatam // 2.237 //
children.translated_text: and from the origination of things, the eternal <s>Brahman</s> is conceived as having a beginning. (2.237)

children.text: asatye vartmani sthitvā % tataḥ satyaṃ samīhate // 2.238 //
children.translated_text: standing on the path of untruth, one then seeks the truth. (2.238)

body.translated_text: The means of instruction for children who are learning are gentle enticements;

children.text: punar vākye tam evārtham % anyathā pratipadyate // 2.239 //
children.translated_text: one then understands that very same meaning differently in the sentence. (2.239)

body.text: upāttā bahavo 'py arthā $ yeṣv ante pratiṣedhanam &

children.text: kriyate te nivartante % tasmāt tāṃs tatra nāśrayet // 2.240 //
children.translated_text: is made — they are turned away; therefore, one should not rely on them there. (2.240)

children.text: nārthe na buddhau saṃbandho % nivṛtter avatiṣṭhate // 2.241 //
children.translated_text: the cessation does not rest in the meaning, nor in the cognition, nor in the relation. (2.241)

body.translated_text: The sentence 'the tree does not exist' characterizes the absence of a qualified entity;

children.text: aśabdavācyā sā buddhir % nivartyeta sthitā katham // 2.242 //
children.translated_text: how would that cognition, which is inexpressible by words, be negated while remaining? (2.242)

body.translated_text: And in the analytic understanding, if one determines 'it exists,'

children.translated_text: but if that itself is its substrate, then the Vedic usage would be for the purpose of restriction. (2.244)

body.translated_text: Or, for the purpose of indicating restriction, it would be like a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>);

children.translated_text: as is construed by analyzing the individual words. (2.247)

children.translated_text: that is an approach to the sentence-meaning in conveying a single meaning. (2.248)

body.translated_text: Or, if the meaning resides in the words without being combined,

body.text: pūrvaṃ padeṣv asaṃsṛṣṭo $ yaḥ kramād upacīyate &

children.translated_text: is known as superior, because it is like something cut and then re-tied. (2.249)

body.translated_text: That which is initially uncombined in the words and is gradually accumulated in sequence,

body.text: ekam āhur anekārthaṃ $ śabdam anye parīkṣakāḥ &

children.translated_text: the universality of a single word is differentiated by the difference of determining factors. (2.250)

body.translated_text: Other investigators say a single word has many meanings;

children.translated_text: either through context and topic, or through connection with another word. (2.251)

body.translated_text: Going beyond simultaneity, a word settles into alternation,

children.text: tathā sa eva gośabdo % vāhīke 'pi vyavasthitaḥ // 2.252 //
children.translated_text: so that very same word 'go' is also established in the sense of a Vāhīka (a type of people). (2.252)

children.translated_text: from the difference in familiarity arise its secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>) and primary (<s>mukhya</s>) senses. (2.253)

body.translated_text: But since that very word possesses all powers and has multiple properties,

body.translated_text: Similarly, one <s>mantra</s> applies to the self (<s>adhyātma</s>), to the deity (<s>adhidaiva</s>), and to the ritual (<s>adhikratu</s>),

children.translated_text: only the meaning is reversed — the word remains established in its own meaning. (2.255)

children.translated_text: only the meaning is reversed, but the verbal expression remains fixed in its own form. (2.256)

body.translated_text: Similarly, the own-form of words is connected in all meanings;

children.translated_text: even when there is complete difference, say those who follow the path of distinction. (2.257)

children.translated_text: and different from that in the series of recitations — yet it is perceived as one and the same. (2.261)

children.text: yuktaḥ pratyāyayaty arthaṃ % taṃ gauṇam apare viduḥ // 2.264 //

children.translated_text: the connection with another word is possible for only one [meaning]. // 2.269 //

children.translated_text: some even consider excess as deficiency with respect to conventional usage in certain cases. // 2.272 //

children.translated_text: others know that as secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>), based on a property similar to the related [class]. // 2.273 //

children.translated_text: but their fitness [for a particular action] is understood as restricted by form alone, // 2.276 //

body.translated_text: In the <s>cvi</s>-derivative sense of [words like] <s>go</s>, <s>yuṣmad</s>, <s>mahat</s>, when there is a shift from one's own meaning to another,

body.translated_text: The original form (<s>prakṛti</s>) acquires greatness and whiteness;

body.translated_text: Words like <s>Agni</s> (fire) and <s>Soma</s>, which have their own form as their referent,

body.text: agnidattas tu yo 'gniḥ syāt $ tatra svārthopasarjanaḥ &

children.translated_text: but due to the difference of touch and other [senses], water is not a mirage. // 2.287 //

body.translated_text: The distinctive effect that is well-known for a rope and a snake respectively —
